results.description: Throwback observation of the inciting incident for my career. This is one of the first Burmese python breeding aggregations captured in Key Largo. At least two individuals are seen in a subterranean cavern in Dagny Johnson Key Largo Hammock Botanical State Park. This event was captured because a scout python, "Sal", was spending a weird amount of time in a rockpile in the park. I set up a few cameras and observed him exiting rockpile and then very shortly after exiting again. I started comparing the dorsal patterns of the photos and found Sal was not alone! In the length of Crocodile Lake's scout python program, this was the only instance of a scout python leading to the successful location of an associate python. Unfortunately, the rockpile they were inhabiting was gigantic with boulders several hundred pounds in mass. We did we could to push them off but found that the rocks were covering the entrance to a massive cave network snaking into multiple directions. We staked out that area for weeks hoping to capture the associate and set up several other camera traps but there were too many portals to cover. At the main entrance we were working, we captured this mating event. Shortly after this however, Sal was found "basking" outside of the cave entrance. We approached and he was not basking, but instead dead. No idea what was the cause but at least he went out with a bang I guess. A few days later, a third python showed up. Neither the female nor the third confirmed python were ever recovered but years later I still check that spot every so often. One of the coolest things I have ever witnessed working here.
